items.title: Alan Raph interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001
items.q: Jimmy Cleveland and I were on a rock & roll date where we could hardly play

ctx.x: That’s great. You actually got paid to laugh that hard. Well did you get paid, I don’t know.

Jimmy Cleveland and I were on a rock & roll date where we could hardly play, we were breaking each other up with comments about the music and everything. And we finally got to the point where it was really a struggle to just play. I don’t think we worked for that guy again.
Yeah. What was it — you’re not buying it you’re selling it. A little hard to remember that in those situations.
